cd /home/mike/nexus-wt/cs10b && git push -q -u origin v1/cs10-docker-files-worker 2>&1 | tail -1; gh pr create --base main --head v1/cs10-docker-files-worker --title "feat(cli,core): worker inside Docker; separate files-only worker with no network (CS-10 Docker and phase 2)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why
Owner gate decision (2026-11-21): CS-10's remainder is required for v1.2.2. Phase 1 (#664) confined the native worker under Bubblewrap only; `--sandbox docker` still left the worker with the operator's access, and the parsing surface shared the command worker's network.

## What
**Docker.** On Linux, `--sandbox docker` runs `harness-core` as the long-lived process of one hardened container (`docker run --interactive --init`, built from the same arguments a sandboxed command gets). The host-built (glibc) worker is mounted read-only at `/nexus-worker` with its ELF interpreter and the libraries `ldd` reports and started through that interpreter, so the pinned Alpine image is not modified. Commands run inside the container with the image's `sh` (as the per-command wrap did) and are not wrapped a second time. Fails closed; plain `--sandbox` tries Bubblewrap, then Docker, then behaves as before. A daemon check keeps "CLI installed, daemon down" from breaking file tools in auto mode.

**Phase 2 (design option B).** With a sandboxed worker, every method except `run_command`, `cancel`, `end_background`, `list_services` goes to a second worker started with `--files-only`. The core refuses those four methods in that mode and reports `files_only` in `hello`; the CLI will not use a files worker that does not report it. Its sandbox is built with the network off regardless of `--sandbox-network`. The command worker starts on the first command. Bridge state moved into a per-process channel object to allow two workers.

## Behaviour changes
- `--sandbox docker` on Linux now refuses to start the worker outside a container.
- With a containerised worker, a session's commands share one container (and its `/tmp`) instead of each getting a new one.
- Non-Linux hosts: unchanged (Docker confines commands only; `doctor` says so).

## Limits (also in the design note, section 10)
The files worker's refusal is a check inside the process; what holds under compromise is its sandbox (no network, no path outside the workspace). The two workers share the workspace. Option C (Landlock/seccomp) is not built.

## Verification
- `core/tests/files_only_worker.rs` (3): refusal of each command method with the refused command not run, baseline without the flag, one-shot `call` path. `cargo test --release` all green; clippy clean.
- `cli/test/worker_isolation.test.ts` 24/24 on Node 24 with Bubblewrap and a real Docker daemon: canary under `$HOME` unreadable, writes outside refused, no network by default and never for the files worker, no container survives shutdown, fail-closed paths, daemon-down fallback, stand-in old core refused for the files role.
- Mutation checks (each makes named tests fail): files worker given the operator's network (2 fail); no `sh` for a containerised worker (1); handshake role check removed (1); routing to the files worker removed (3).
- Also green: `doctor` 60, `harness` 90, `sandbox_docker` 12, `sandbox_confine` 13, `sandbox_cancel` 2, `readonly_command_paths` 36, `fault_kill_mid_tool_call`, `check_requirements --enforce`, leak check.
- Not run locally: Node 22 (not installed on this host); CI's `test-matrix (22)` covers it.

## Reference coding
XERJ queried (`xerj code opencode "docker container sandbox spawn worker ..."`, `"bubblewrap bwrap landlock seccomp sandbox process"`): weak or unrelated matches only; the indexed corpus has no containerised-worker analogue. Nothing taken. The loader-in-a-private-directory approach follows this repo's own precedent of mounting a binary's individual ELF dependencies (`appendRuntimeFile` in `cli/src/sandbox.ts`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

# VC-9: headless needs-input audit

Date: 2026-11-18. Base: origin/main `b1b74858` (file:line below are at that commit; the glue added by this change is listed in the last column).
Reference: Anthropic 2026 agentic coding trends report, trend 4 (agents that learn when to ask for help).

A headless run has no operator (`onConfirm` absent). This lists every place it needs a human decision, what happens today, and what this change does about it. Outcomes today: **stalls** = the model gets a plain error and carries on or the turn ends with nothing structured; **guesses** = a decision is made on the operator's behalf. No path ended BLOCKED with a question before this change (`grep needs_input cli/src` fo

The shared shape added: turn `execution=BLOCKED`, `reason=NEEDS_INPUT`, `needsInput = { id, kind, prompt, subject, options[approve|decline] }` (`cli/src/core/needs_input.ts`, `cli/src/core/turn.ts`), and `nexus run --resume <task> --answer <id>=approve|decline`.

| # | Path | Where the decision is needed (base) | Today | After this change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tool needs approval (write, exec, egress) in review mode (the headless default) | `cli/src/core/dispatch_tool_call.ts:258-293` | stalls: receipt `DENIED / DECISION_REQUIRED_NO_OPERATOR`, plain error to the model, which works around it | BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT `tool_approval`; `--answer` approves that exact call once |
| 2 | Egress approval | same site, `effect === "egress"` (`dispatch_tool_call.ts:259-264`) | stalls (as 1); under `--yes` it is approved without asking, by explicit opt-in | as 1 |
| 3 | Verification-file or test edit (Makefile, CI, test files, package scripts) | `cli/src/security.ts:811` (`ctx.operator ? "ask" : "deny"`), refused at `dispatch_tool_call.ts:198-227` | stalls: `VERIFICATION_CONFIG_PROTECTED`, "none was given", model continues | BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT `verification_edit` for the decision case (not for policy mode `block`, which is a rule, not a decision); `--answer` approves that p
| 4 | Verifier approval at `task_completed` | `cli/src/core/spine_handlers.ts:180-197`, gate `cli/src/core/completion_oracle.ts:37-40` (`if (!onConfirm) return false`) | stalls: tool error to the model | BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT `verifier_approval` (id binds command and script digest). The pre-change baseline captures do not ask |
| 5 | Requirement-declared verifier approval | `completion_oracle.ts:213-216` | stalls: string returned, verifier skipped | as 4 |
| 6 | Type-check approval (CG-4, VC-6) | `completion_oracle.ts:84-87` | stalls: enforce mode blocks with text; record mode silently skips | as 4, for an enforced type-check; a record-only one is still just not run |
| 7 | Steering that negates a requirement | `cli/src/agent.ts:1912-1921` (`conflict.status = "unresolved"` when no `onConfirm`), reachable only through the sidecar (`cli/src/sidecar.ts:376`) | stalls: conflict stays `unresolved`, steering not applied (no guess), nothing at turn level | **not done**: see "Not done" |
| 8 | Requirement marked `blocked` by the model | `cli/src/core/objective.ts:500,561`; turn at `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts:1308,1349` | stalls: `COMPLETED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`, reason only in a note | **not done**: see "Not done" |
| 9 | Egress secret block | `cli/src/tools.ts:1226` (`EGRESS_SECRET_BLOCKED`) | policy denial, not a decision (allow-list is operator config) | out of scope by design |
| 10 | Injection-suspicion approval | `dispatch_tool_call.ts:228` (`Boolean(onConfirm) && ...`) | not asked headless; the normal policy applies | no change: it is an extra prompt, not a missing decision |
| 11 | Workspace trust | `cli/src/startup_trust.ts:136-141` | non-TTY: continues `untrusted` (instructions and integrations unloaded, noted) | no change: degraded, not blocked; trust never widens authority |
| 12 | Verifier not converging / tool-call loop | `run_turn.ts:1244-1252` | already BLOCKED, but no question or answer path | no change here (a decision to stop, not a yes/no) |
| 13 | Operation work unit BLOCKED | `cli/src/core/scheduler.ts:360-440`, `nexus operation decide` | already BLOCKED + question + resume (reference implementation) | no change |
| 14 | Subagent hits 1-6 | `spine_handlers.ts:482`, `cli/src/synthesizer.ts:243-307` | stalls inside the child | `spawn_subagent`: the child stops at the question and returns it in its result (same id and shape as a parent-originated one, plus `subagent: { depth, objective }`); the parent ends BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT with it. Other child paths (`/team`, operations) already run as scheduled work units, not in-turn: no c

No ask-the-user tool, plan approval, git push confirmation or MCP elicitation exists in `cli/src` (searched), so there is no further path.

## Behaviour notes

- A question stops the turn at the call that raised it; later calls in the same batch are reported as not executed.
- An answer is bound to the decision: the id is a digest of the tool and arguments (1, 2), the path and tool (3), or the command and script digest (4-6). A different action gets a different id and asks again.
- `approve` covers the one action. `decline` is recorded for the run and the action is refused without asking again.
- Exit code stays 1 for BLOCKED; machine consumers read `turn.reason` and `turn.needsInput` (`--json`, stream-json `result`).
- Answers live in the invoking process. Resuming without `--answer` asks again.

## Not done (needs a design decision)

- **7 (steering conflict)** only occurs through the sidecar, which already has a client that can resolve the conflict. Ending the turn BLOCKED requires deciding what the sidecar protocol does with a BLOCKED turn and whether an `unresolved` conflict may be resolved after the fact (`resolveSteeringConflict` accepts only `pending`).
- **8 (blocked requirement)** currently ends `COMPLETED / REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`, and operations, continuation and several tests depend on that. Changing it to BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT changes an existing contract (reason, execution, exit code) and the answer is free text (what to do about the blocker), not approve/decline.

## Subagents (row 14)

A headless in-turn subagent (`spawn_subagent`, depth 1) that needs a decision records the question on itself (`subagentQuestions`), stops at the call that raised it (it does not wait, take the decision or route around it) and returns it in `SubagentResult.needsInput`. The parent records it through `acceptSubagentQuestions`: the first becomes `TurnResult.needsInput`; further distinct questions go to `TurnResult.furthe

Limits, stated plainly: the child is not resumed, it is spawned again from the model's next `spawn_subagent` call, so work it did before the question is redone (workspace changes it already made stay); resume depends on the model delegating the same way again. Questions are listed only when one call raised several (a batch stops at the first recorded question, so a second `spawn_subagent` in the same batch does not r

new='''## Rows 7 and 8, done 2026-11-21 (owner gate decision for v1.2.2)

Both were left as design decisions. The owner made them required for v1.2.2; the decisions taken and what was built:

**8, blocked requirement.** Decision: the contract changes for `nexus run` only (`config.surface === "headless"`, top-level agent). There the turn ends `BLOCKED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / NEEDS_INPUT` with `needsInput.kind = "blocked_requirement"` instead of `COMPLETED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`; the durable task status therefore becomes `failed` instead of `completed`, and the exit code stays 1. The REPL, the sidecar, operations and library callers keep `REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE` (an operator or a client is there to read the blocker), and so do requirements that are only still open, or descoped and awaiting acceptance. The answer is free text: the question's only option is `reply`, given as `--answer <id>=reply:<text>` (2000 characters at most, refused rather than cut). The id is a digest of the requirement id and the stated reason. The resumed run passes the reply to the model with an instruction to reopen the requirement or record it descoped; the harness does not change the requirement itself, so a model that leaves it blocked for the same reason gets the same question again. Several blocked requirements: the first is `needsInput`, the others `furtherNeedsInput`. Code: `buildBlockedRequirementQuestion`, `parseOperatorAnswers`, `replyNote` (`cli/src/core/needs_input.ts`), `buildTurnResultImpl` (`cli/src/core/run_turn.ts`). Tests: `cli/test/vc9_blocked_requirement.test.ts`.

**7, steering conflict.** Decisions: (a) an `unresolved` conflict may be decided after the fact (`resolveSteeringConflict` accepts `unresolved` as well as `pending`; nothing was applied in the meantime, and a decided conflict is never decided twice); (b) the sidecar delivers the BLOCKED turn as an ordinary `turn.result` carrying `needsInput`, and gains one command, `answer` (`question`, `option`), for clients with no live approval prompt; resending the steering and deciding at the prompt still works. Behaviour: a turn that would otherwise report completion, during which a conflict ended undecided (nobody could be asked, or the turn closed first), ends `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT` with `kind = "steering_conflict"`, options approve and decline, id bound to the steering message. An interrupted or failed turn keeps its own result. At the next turn's start an answer is applied (approve: the requirements are descoped as accepted and the steering is queued, once; decline: nothing changes) and conflicts without an answer are marked `carried`, so only the turn that left a conflict undecided reports it. Code: `buildSteeringConflictQuestion`, `carryUnresolvedConflicts` (`cli/src/core/objective.ts`), `cli/src/protocol.ts`, `cli/src/sidecar.ts`. Tests: `cli/test/vc9_steering_conflict.test.ts`.

Limits, stated plainly: answers live in the invoking process (as for rows 1 to 6); a new objective starts a new ledger, so an old conflict can no longer be answered; the Rust TUI shows the BLOCKED turn but has no key for `answer` (resend the steering there); a descoped requirement awaiting acceptance in a headless run is still `REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`, not a question.

## Why
Owner gate decision (2026-11-21): VC-9's two remaining cases are required for v1.2.2. The audit (`docs/v1.2.1/VC-9-needs-input-audit.md`) left both as design decisions; the decisions taken are recorded there under "Rows 7 and 8".

## What
**Row 8, blocked requirement (contract change, `nexus run` only).** When the model marks an operator requirement blocked, a headless run ends `BLOCKED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / NEEDS_INPUT` with `needsInput.kind = "blocked_requirement"` instead of `COMPLETED / REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`. The only option is `reply`; the operator answers in free text with `--answer <id>=reply:<text>` (2000 characters at most), and the resumed run gives the reply to the model. The id binds the requirement and its stated reason. REPL, sidecar, operations and library callers are unchanged, as are requirements that are only open or descoped-awaiting-acceptance.

**Row 7, steering conflict.** A turn that would otherwise report completion, during which steering that drops a requirement ended undecided, ends `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT` (`kind = "steering_conflict"`, approve/decline). An unresolved conflict can now be decided after the fact: the answer is applied at the next turn's start (approve descopes the requirements as accepted and queues the steering once). Conflicts without an answer are marked `carried`, so only the turn that left one undecided reports it. Sidecar: the BLOCKED turn is an ordinary `turn.result`; one new command, `answer`.

## Contract changes
- `nexus run` with a blocked requirement: `execution` COMPLETED -> BLOCKED, `reason` REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE -> NEEDS_INPUT, task status `completed` -> `failed`; exit code stays 1.
- A turn with an undecided steering conflict: result becomes BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT (an interrupted or failed turn keeps its own result).
- `resolveSteeringConflict` accepts `unresolved`; `SteeringConflict.carried` added; `NeedsInputQuestion.options` may carry `reply`.

## Verification
- `cli/test/vc9_blocked_requirement.test.ts` (10) and `cli/test/vc9_steering_conflict.test.ts` (13), real agent loop against the local gateway fixture; each behaviour has a baseline (other surfaces, operator present, non-conflicting steer, no answer).
- Mutation checks: question raised on every surface (1 fails); descoped treated as blocked (1); steering question removed (5); carried conflict re-asked (1); unresolved not decidable (5).
- Unchanged and green: `vc9_needs_input` 14, `vc9_subagent_needs_input` 13, `si3_steering_conflict` 26, `sidecar` 63, `sidecar_steering_diff` 19, `sidecar_projection` 23, `objective_continuation` 42, `independent_verification` 33, `sidecar_surface` 4, `tsc`, `check_requirements --enforce`, leak check.
- Not run locally: Node 22 (not installed on this host; CI covers it).

## Limits
Answers live in the invoking process. A new objective starts a new ledger, so an old conflict can no longer be answered. The Rust TUI shows the BLOCKED turn but has no key for `answer` (resend the steering there). `cli/src/agent.ts` is untouched (held by another lane); the turn-start hook lives in `run_turn.ts`.

## Reference coding
Extends this repo's own VC-9 mechanism (`needs_input.ts`); no peer-project analogue consulted for the ledger rules. XERJ not queried for this change: the design is fixed by the existing audit and question shape.

# /loop
Parse input as `[interval] <prompt>`: a first token matching ^\d+[smhd]$ is the interval; else a trailing `every <N> <unit>` (only when a time follows "every"); else no interval (dynamic). Empty prompt → print `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

## Fixed interval
Cron: Nm≤59 → `*/N * * * *`; Nm≥60 or Nh → `0 */H * * *`; Nd → `0 0 */N * *`; Ns → round up to minutes. Round uneven intervals to the nearest clean one and say so. CronCreate (recurring: true), confirm cadence + job ID in one line (expires after 7 days; cancel with CronDelete), then run the prompt now.

1. Run the prompt now (slash command → Skill tool).
2. If the next run waits on an event, arm one Monitor (timeout_ms 1800000) unless TaskList shows one running.

# CX-4: tool-output masking, measured (2026-11-21)

**Result:** with `NEXUS_TOOL_OUTPUT_MASK_TOKENS=2000`, every run still passed and the prompt tokens sent to the model roughly
halved. **Decision for v1.2.2: masking stays opt-in; 2000 is the documented recommended value.** A default is deferred until
it is measured on more than one model (see "Why not a default yet").

## Method

- Tasks: `cx4-verbose-fix` (a test runner printing about 1000 lines per run), `cx4-log-triage` (the cause on two lines of a
  6000-line log), `cx4-wide-rename` (a helper renamed across 18 files). Each has a hidden behavioural check and a regression
  command; they are generated by `eval/gen_cx4_tasks.py` and are not part of core-v1.
- Arms: `eval/configs/cx4-unmasked.json` and `eval/configs/cx4-masked-2000.json` (the same config plus
  `toolOutputMaskTokens: 2000`), run by `eval/run_cx4_measurement.sh`, 5 runs per task per arm, one at a time, under the
  GATEWAY claim, 05:47 to 06:41 UTC.
- Model: gateway alias `engineering/lead`, 65536 context. The same built agent binary served both arms (one executable
  SHA-256 across all 30 records).
- Per-run records: [`cx4-masking-measurement-2026-11-21.json`](cx4-masking-measurement-2026-11-21.json).

## Observed

| Task | Arm | Hidden check | Regression | Prompt tokens, median (min to max) | Wall seconds, median (min to max) | Steps, median |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `cx4-log-triage` | unmasked | 5/5 | 5/5 | 229,883 (144,013 to 289,251) | 124 (94 to 152) | 11 |
| `cx4-log-triage` | masked 2000 | 5/5 | 5/5 | 133,214 (107,778 to 174,506) | 77 (62 to 91) | 11 |
| `cx4-verbose-fix` | unmasked | 5/5 | 5/5 | 183,937 (179,987 to 279,477) | 63 (53 to 204) | 7 |
| `cx4-verbose-fix` | masked 2000 | 5/5 | 5/5 | 84,294 (76,549 to 94,488) | 58 (58 to 62) | 8 |
| `cx4-wide-rename` | unmasked | 5/5 | 5/5 | 230,357 (111,197 to 282,308) | 61 (34 to 563) | 9 |
| `cx4-wide-rename` | masked 2000 | 5/5 | 5/5 | 90,866 (74,298 to 234,708) | 51 (39 to 107) | 8 |

Median prompt tokens fell by 42%, 54% and 61%. No run timed out in either arm. Step counts did not rise, so the model did
not visibly pay for masking with extra re-reads on these tasks.

## What this does and does not show

- It shows no correctness cost and a large input-token saving on three large-output tasks, on one model, at one threshold.
- It does not show safety in general. All 30 runs passed, so the tasks did not discriminate: they cannot reveal a task on
  which masking loses needed evidence. Five runs per cell cannot bound a rare failure.
- Wall time is a weak signal here: the two long unmasked `cx4-wide-rename` runs (414 s and 563 s) are outliers that may be
  gateway load.
- The harness reported every run as `UNVERIFIED` or `NOT_ESTABLISHED` (the agent finished without running its own
  verification) in both arms; pass and fail above are the hidden and regression checks, not the agent's claim.
- The two arms ran back to back, not interleaved, so a drift in gateway behaviour during the hour would be confounded with
  the arm.

## Why not a default yet

The gateway serves two distinct models (`docs/evidence/v1.2.2/WM-3-gateway-aliases.md`) and only one was measured; other
thresholds were not tried; and the tasks all passed. Turning masking on by default changes what every user's model sees, so
it needs a measurement that could have failed: `engineering/deep`, at least one harder task where an early output must be
recalled verbatim late in the run, and interleaved arms. Until then the feature is opt-in, with 2000 as the value that has
evidence behind it.

## Why
Owner gate decision (2026-11-21): CS-10's remainder is required for v1.2.2. Phase 1 (#664) confined the native worker under Bubblewrap only; `--sandbox docker` still left the worker with the operator's access, and the parsing surface shared the command worker's network.

## What
**Docker.** On Linux, `--sandbox docker` runs `harness-core` as the long-lived process of one hardened container (`docker run --interactive --init`, built from the same arguments a sandboxed command gets). The host-built (glibc) worker is mounted read-only at `/nexus-worker` with its ELF interpreter and the libraries `ldd` reports and started through that interpreter, so the pinned Alpine image is not modified. Commands run inside the container with the image's `sh` (as the per-command wrap did) and are not wrapped a second time. Fails closed; plain `--sandbox` tries Bubblewrap, then Docker, then behaves as before. A daemon check keeps "CLI installed, daemon down" from breaking file tools in auto mode.

**Phase 2 (design option B).** With a sandboxed worker, every method except `run_command`, `cancel`, `end_background`, `list_services` goes to a second worker started with `--files-only`. The core refuses those four methods in that mode and reports `files_only` in `hello`; the CLI will not use a files worker that does not report it. Its sandbox is built with the network off regardless of `--sandbox-network`. The command worker starts on the first command. Bridge state moved into a per-process channel object to allow two workers.

## Behaviour changes
- `--sandbox docker` on Linux now refuses to start the worker outside a container.
- With a containerised worker, a session's commands share one container (and its `/tmp`) instead of each getting a new one.
- Non-Linux hosts: unchanged (Docker confines commands only; `doctor` says so).

## Limits (also in the design note, section 10)
The files worker's refusal is a check inside the process; what holds under compromise is its sandbox (no network, no path outside the workspace). The two workers share the workspace. Option C (Landlock/seccomp) is not built.

## Why
Owner gate decision (2026-11-21): VC-9's two remaining cases are required for v1.2.2. The audit (`docs/v1.2.1/VC-9-needs-input-audit.md`) left both as design decisions; the decisions taken are recorded there under "Rows 7 and 8".

## What
**Row 8, blocked requirement (contract change, `nexus run` only).** When the model marks an operator requirement blocked, a headless run ends `BLOCKED / NOT_ESTABLISHED / NEEDS_INPUT` with `needsInput.kind = "blocked_requirement"` instead of `COMPLETED / REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`. The only option is `reply`; the operator answers in free text with `--answer <id>=reply:<text>` (2000 characters at most), and the resumed run gives the reply to the model. The id binds the requirement and its stated reason. REPL, sidecar, operations and library callers are unchanged, as are requirements that are only open or descoped-awaiting-acceptance.

**Row 7, steering conflict.** A turn that would otherwise report completion, during which steering that drops a requirement ended undecided, ends `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT` (`kind = "steering_conflict"`, approve/decline). An unresolved conflict can now be decided after the fact: the answer is applied at the next turn's start (approve descopes the requirements as accepted and queues the steering once). Conflicts without an answer are marked `carried`, so only the turn that left one undecided reports it. Sidecar: the BLOCKED turn is an ordinary `turn.result`; one new command, `answer`.

## Contract changes
- `nexus run` with a blocked requirement: `execution` COMPLETED -> BLOCKED, `reason` REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE -> NEEDS_INPUT, task status `completed` -> `failed`; exit code stays 1.
- A turn with an undecided steering conflict: result becomes BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT (an interrupted or failed turn keeps its own result).
- `resolveSteeringConflict` accepts `unresolved`; `SteeringConflict.carried` added; `NeedsInputQuestion.options` may carry `reply`.

- `cli/test/vc9_blocked_requirement.test.ts` (10) and `cli/test/vc9_steering_conflict.test.ts` (13), real agent loop against the local gateway fixture; each behaviour has a baseline (other surfaces, operator present, non-conflicting steer, no answer).

- Not run locally: Node 22 (not installed on this host; CI covers it).

## Limits
Answers live in the invoking process. A new objective starts a new ledger, so an old conflict can no longer be answered. The Rust TUI shows the BLOCKED turn but has no key for `answer` (resend the steering there). `cli/src/agent.ts` is untouched (held by another lane); the turn-start hook lives in `run_turn.ts`.

v1.2.2 is not released, and I did not merge #672. Codex took the VC-9 claims while I was waiting on its re-run, and the repo's rules don't let me act under a live claim.

## Where things stand

| Gate item | PR | State | Owner now |
|---|---|---|---|
| VC-9: two blocked cases | #672 | Green on all three required checks at `22c2debf`, not merged | Codex |
| CS-10: Docker and phase 2 | #671 | Latest run at `bcb75206` failed; not investigated by me | Codex |
| CS-6: real-server paths | #670 | Merged | done |
| PC-1: CI under 40 minutes | #669 | Sharding merged; new 20-run sample still owed | Codex |

- **#672 is ready to merge.** Its head contains the current `main` (`308635d0`, CI green) and has no file overlap. I logged that for Codex so it can merge without redoing the verification.
- **It needed one re-run.** `test-matrix (24)` failed once on a single test out of 2,418, `vc9_subagent_needs_input`. That test is intermittent on plain `main` too (2 failures in 8 local runs), so it predates my change. The cause is a racy worktree lookup that came in with the delegation work in #668. I logged it as a finding for that lane and did not patch it.
- **A stale green was avoided.** #672's first green run had tested against an older `main`, so I merged the current `main` in and re-ran before treating it as mergeable.

## What I own now
No open gate item is mine any more. Both PRs I built were taken over by Codex, #671 under a handoff its claim records as authorised by you. The VC-9 takeover has no log entry.

## Next
When #671, #672 and the PC-1 sample are on `main` and its CI is green, I'll cut `v1.2.2-rc.1` and run the tool-call matrix on its archive for `deep` and `lead-reasoning`, as you chose. I'll skip that if Codex has claimed the release by then; nobody has so far. The stable tag follows only if the RC meets the 99.5% bar.

I'll check again at 14:43.

# /loop
Parse input as `[interval] <prompt>`: a first token matching ^\d+[smhd]$ is the interval; else a trailing `every <N> <unit>` (only when a time follows "every"); else no interval (dynamic). Empty prompt → print `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

import json,statistics as st
from datetime import datetime as D
p=lambda s:D.fromisoformat(s.replace('Z','+00:00'))
T=p("2026-11-21T10:42:20Z")
runs=[r for r in json.load(open('/tmp/claude-1000/pc1.json')) if r['status']=='completed' and r['conclusion']!='cancelled' and p(r['createdAt'])>T]
runs.sort(key=lambda r:r['createdAt'],reverse=True)
first20=sorted(runs,key=lambda r:r['createdAt'])[:20]   # the first 20 after the change, fixed set
first20.sort(key=lambda r:r['createdAt'],reverse=True)
def el(r): return (p(r['updatedAt'])-p(r['createdAt'])).total_seconds()
f=lambda s:"%d:%02d"%(s//60,s%60)
e=[el(r) for r in first20]
single=[el(r) for r in first20 if r.get('attempt',1)==1]
ok=sum(r['conclusion']=='success' for r in first20)
print(len(runs),len(first20),f(st.median(e)),f(min(e)),f(max(e)),ok,len(single),f(st.median(single)),f(max(single)), sum(x<2400 for x in e))
rows="\n".join(f"| {r['databaseId']} | `{r['headSha'][:8]}` | {r['conclusion']} | {f(el(r))} | {r.get('attempt',1)} | {r['displayTitle'][:70]} |" for r in first20)
doc=f"""# PC-1 PR CI after test sharding

Collected: 2026-11-21 {D.utcnow().strftime('%H:%M')} UTC

**Result: the median PR CI time is {f(st.median(e))}, under the plan's 40-minute target** (baseline 42:19, `PC-1_BASELINE_2026-11-20.md`).

- Change measured: PR #669 (`perf(ci): shard cli suite within existing jobs`), merged 2026-11-21T10:42:20Z as `625d1e4c`. The CLI suite runs as two concurrent shards inside the existing jobs; no job was added or removed, and the required check names are unchanged.
- Source and method: the same as the baseline. GitHub Actions workflow `ci.yml`, `pull_request` events, completed and not cancelled; elapsed is `updatedAt - createdAt`, so it includes queue time.
- Sample: the first 20 such executions created after the merge (a fixed set, not the latest 20 at collection time). They are execution attempts, not 20 distinct pull requests.
- Results: {ok} successes and {20-ok} failures; median **{f(st.median(e))}**; range **{f(min(e))} to {f(max(e))}**; {sum(x<2400 for x in e)} of 20 under 40:00.
- Reproduction: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --event pull_request --limit 100 --json databaseId,createdAt,updatedAt,status,conclusion,headSha,displayTitle,attempt`; keep `status == completed`, `conclusion != cancelled`, `createdAt > 2026-11-21T10:42:20Z`; take the 20 earliest.

## What this does and does not show

- It shows the acceptance criterion as written: a median under 40 minutes over a 20-run sample after the optimization.
- One row is a re-run: its elapsed time spans a failed attempt plus the re-run of the failed job, which is why it is the maximum. Leaving out rows with more than one attempt, the remaining {len(single)} have a median of {f(st.median(single))} and a maximum of {f(max(single))}.

- **What I said:** #671's first CI run failed on one test out of 2,304, and the Docker worker tests passed there.
- **What is true:** that first run also failed three Docker worker tests, with my original code. The suite runs as two shards, and I read only one shard's summary.

- **What I did about it:** I retracted the wrong notes in the claims log. I also ran one experiment: glibc 2.35's loader starts a binary in that image fine on this host, so the glibc version alone doesn't explain the crash. The cause is still unknown.

#671 is still failing for that reason at `860596ec`, and Codex holds it. If starting the worker through its own loader stays unreliable, the alternative is a statically linked worker for Docker mode. That is a bigger change, and whether it fits v1.2.2 may become a decision for you.

content.text:
The PC-1 evidence is merged as `cdff43ed`, so PC-1 is closed. v1.2.2 is still not released, and the more important news is that `main` is intermittently red.

## `main` CI is intermittently red, and I found the cause
- **Evidence:** the #672 merge `d22004e7` failed `test-matrix (24)` and `linux-x86_64` on one test, `vc9_subagent_needs_input`. It passed on re-run and failed on plain `main` earlier. This will randomly fail required checks on every PR and on the release candidate.
- **Cause:** a real product defect, not test timing. I reproduced it in 5 of 20 local runs, and every failure had the same signature:
  - Saving task state throws `PERSISTENCE_FAILED: Task state worktree path has no selected workspace identity`.
  - A new turn inherits the previous turn's worktree binding, and that worktree directory is already gone. The binding's task id also differs from the new turn's record.
  - The binding is only revalidated when the repo directory name trips the secret classifier's high-entropy check. The test's random temp-directory names do that some of the time.
- **Proof:** fixing the directory name to two high-entropy names failed 5 of 5 runs each. A plain name failed 0 of 5. One other plain-looking name failed 4 of 5, only because my script appended varying process-id digits.
- **Impact:** unconfirmed outside tests. It would need a second in-process turn after a blocked, worktree-isolated turn, in a workspace whose path looks random.
- **Handoff:** the test file and the delegation lane are claimed by Codex, so I wrote this up in full for them in the claims log, with two fix options, and did not touch their file. A test-only mitigation would turn `main` green but hide the defect. That tradeoff is Codex's, or yours, to make.

## Gate status
| Item | State |
|---|---|
| VC-9, CS-6, CX-4, PC-1 | merged |
| CS-10 Docker and phase 2 (#671) | still failing; Codex owns it |
| `main` | intermittently red (above) |

- **#671 retraction:** my Docker worker never worked on the hosted runner. It segfaults with exit 139 inside the pinned Alpine image there, from its first push. I retracted my earlier note that it had passed there.
- **If the loader approach stays unreliable:** the alternative is a statically linked worker for Docker mode. That is a bigger change, and whether it fits v1.2.2 may become a decision for you.

I hold no claims or open PRs now. When #671 is fixed and merged and `main` is green on both CI runs for its head, I cut `v1.2.2-rc.1` and measure it. Stable follows only if it meets the 99.5% bar, and not without your go-ahead.

v1.2.2 is not released. CS-10 (#671) is the last gate item and is still stalled, so I set up a way to get evidence on it without touching Codex's branch.

## What changed
- **The flaky `main` test is fixed.** Codex merged #676, which fixes the stale worktree binding I traced earlier. `main` is now at `917a711c`.
- **#671 has had no CI since 15:12.** Its head conflicts with `main` in the changelog, so GitHub never started its checks. Codex is active on other work but hasn't returned to it.
- **I opened a draft probe, #678.** It is Codex's #671 head merged with `main`, with the changelog conflict resolved by keeping both entries. I won't merge it; it exists to produce a CI result and to offer one commit.

## What the probe found locally
- **A real defect in the CS-10 code:** the worker's stdin had no error handler. If the worker process exits right after launch, the next request raises an uncaught `EPIPE` that would crash the CLI. A container that fails to start does exactly that.
- **Evidence:** `sandbox_quoting` failed 3 of 10 runs with it and 0 of 12 after the fix. A new test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- **Rule bend, logged:** the fix edits `cli/src/tools.ts`, a file Codex holds a claim on, though only on my separate branch. I recorded that in the claims log and left it for Codex to take or discard.
- **The rest passes on that tree:** the worker-isolation suite (27 of 27), the Docker sandbox suite and the type-check.

## What the probe will answer
Whether Codex's latest library fix lets the Docker worker start on the hosted runner, where it has crashed on every earlier head. A watch reports when its three required checks finish.

After that, the release still needs CS-10 merged by its owner and a green `main`. Then I cut `v1.2.2-rc.1` and measure it. I won't tag stable without your go-ahead.

v1.2.1 is published (tag `v1.2.1` = commit b0d59908, version-only child of `v1.2.1-rc.2` = 12cf4912; rc.1 = e1ad87a6 never published an archive). G1.1-4 on the rc.2 archive: `engineering/deep` 200/200 and `engineering/lead-reasoning` 200/200 native valid, one run, only 2 of 5 gateway aliases (evidence `docs/evidence/v1.2.1/`). Deferred with reasons in `docs/v1.2.1/PLAN.md` "Release disposition": MQ-1/MQ-2, MQ-4, RD-1/RD-2, PC-1 (CI 37-45 min), MT-3 part, WM-3 partial.

**Why:** the rc.1 release workflow failed in the CLI suite step on a host-conditional test (`cs4_shell_audit` exit-127 hint: skipped where `/usr/bin/cargo` exists, so PR CI never ran it; release runner has >12 toolchain-looking env vars, hint shows only first 12 sorted). Tags are immutable, so it advanced to rc.2. See [[version-tags-immutable]].

**How to apply (release flow that works):**
- Release-prep PR: bump root `package.json`, run `node scripts/sync-version.mjs`, add `docs/releases/<tag>.md` for the RC AND the stable version (stable commit must be version-only), changelog heading dated. `docs/releases/LATEST` + README status/pins move only in a manual follow-up PR after the stable is published (`scripts/check_doc_versions.mjs`).
- Tag signed (`git tag -s`, key already configured) on the PR merge commit whose tree equals the green head (confirm `head` contains main). The release workflow reruns the full CLI suite, security gates, two reproducible packages, SBOM, smokes, attestation (~1h). It runs tests PR CI skips, so run host-conditional tests under a flooded env before tagging.
- Stable: branch from the rc tag commit, one version-only commit (`scripts/check-version-only-diff.mjs <rc> HEAD`), merge via PR with a merge commit (must be an ancestor of main), tag the branch commit (parent must carry the `-rc.N` tag). Stable tag builds a DRAFT; verify checksums, `gh attestation verify`, compare with the RC archive, public-install test, then `gh release edit --draft=false`.
- G1.1-4: follow `docs/v1.1.4/G1.1-4-LIVE-MATRIX.md` (GATEWAY claim, throwaway HOME, installer install with `NEXUS_VERIFY_ATTESTATION=1`, per-alias `limits_version` from /v1/models, key var `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY` mapped to `apiKeyEnv`, max_tokens 8192, interval 1200 ms); ~47 min for two aliases; record unaltered.
- CI polling: a running job has an empty `conclusion`, so test `status/conclusion == COMPLETED/SUCCESS` for all four required checks (test-matrix 22, 24, linux-x86_64, CodeQL); PR CI takes ~40-45 min.

**Post-release work (2026-11-18, PRs #601-#617, all merged):** CX-7/CX-6, WM-3 (all five gateway aliases, reasoning-off aliases show `passed:false` only for the hybrid-reasoning check), PC-4/6/7 + DH-6 (`check_requirements --enforce` now in test-matrix), MT-3 part, VC-2 (+completion wiring), VC-3 part, VC-6, VC-7, VC-9 part (headless review mode now ends BLOCKED/NEEDS_INPUT, top-level only), CX-4 opt-in, RD-6 (+`--fork-session`), CS-5, CS-11 (gap: command erroring with changing text not stopped), CS-6 (found + fixed a real bug: default TS/JS/Python LSP launch lacked `--stdio`; hosted run: ts/pyright/gopls pass, rust-analyzer fails to start under the product launch, kept as todo), MQ-3 (hosted run validated after a pip --user/HOME fix), MQ-4 (built, not scheduled or run live). Backlog for the rest: `docs/v1.2.2/BACKLOG.md`.

**Lessons:** agent PRs need local runs with `FORCE_COLOR=1 CI=true` and all affected suites (CI found failures in 3 of the agent PRs that their local subsets missed); re-run an agent's mutation claims yourself (one survived, one was falsely reported); agents can stall for hours behind their own watcher loops, so give foreground-only rules; resolve merge conflicts in EVERY conflicted file (a PLAN.md marker was committed once, caught by `git diff --check`); a hosted first run of a new workflow often finds setup bugs (HOME isolation vs `pip --user`).

## What
The native worker's `stdin` stream had no `error` listener. A request written after the process was already gone raises `EPIPE` on the stream asynchronously; with no listener that is an uncaught exception that ends the CLI. After this change the request waiting on that worker is answered as a disconnect.

Reachable in production with the CS-10 Docker worker: a container that fails to start exits at once, and the next tool call writes to its closed stdin.

## Evidence
- New `cli/test/worker_stdin_epipe.test.ts` (a stand-in worker that exits immediately, 25 rounds of 3 concurrent requests, asserts no uncaught exception and no success): **fails 3 of 3 without the change, passes 3 of 3 with it.**
- Found while probing CS-10 (#671): on that branch `sandbox_quoting` failed 3 of 10 local runs from the same uncaught `EPIPE`. On current `main` that suite did not fail in 12 runs without this change, so I am not claiming it fixes a flake there; the new test is the evidence.
- Green on this tree: `worker_isolation` 27, `sandbox_docker` 12, `harness` 90, leak check, `tsc`. Probe PR #678 (the same commit on top of the CS-10 head) passed all three required checks.
- Not run locally: Node 22 (not installed on this host); CI covers it.

## Change surface
`cli/src/tools.ts` (7 lines) and the new test file only. The file's claim still names the CS-10 holder, whose PR has merged; recorded in the claims log at 17:2x UTC.

## Reference coding
Not applicable (a missing stream error listener).

### Added | - Significant independent reviews now require eight non-empty engineering-assessment fields when a diff touches core code, five or more files, or at least 300 added/removed lines. Prefix rules decide a shell command as `allow` (no prompt in review mode), `prompt` (asks even in auto mode, unless `--yes`) or `forbidden` (refused in every mode); the strictes
### Added | - VC-2: an authorised regression obligation is discharged only when the verifier output reports a recognised result for that exact test. A green suite that does not show the test, a skipped result, and older pass records without test-name binding remain unresolved and block completion.
### Added | - CS-11: a command that fails with only volatile text changing (a retry counter, request or job number, ephemeral port, temp directory name, counter after a transfer verb, compound duration; an HTTP status, a build step index and outcome counts stay distinct) is now the same failure to the non-progr
### Added | - VC-9: a delegated subagent's headless decision (tool approval, verification-file edit, verifier approval) is no longer lost. The subagent stops at it and returns the question (same id and shape, plus `subagent: { depth, objective }`) to its parent, whose headless run ends BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT; `-

They are now registered after connection as `extension` capa
### Fixed | - The real language-server job's Rust setup: rust-analyzer is now added to the default toolchain (the product launches servers outside the repository, where the repository's pinned toolchain does not apply), and the test's availability probe runs in the fixture directory, as the product does.
### Fixed | - `lsp_diagnostics` for Rust no longer reports a file with type errors as clean: rust-analyzer sends an empty first `publishDiagnostics` before it has loaded the Cargo project and analysed types, and the client returned on it. Servers that analyse in stages are marked `awaitProgress` (rust-analyzer

### Added | - Behavioural differential against a declared reference (plan unit VC-3, rest): `/requirements differential <R> --inputs <file>` runs the objective's latest verifier command and the operator-authorised reference command on each input (a JSON array of at most 50 strings, each at most 64 KiB) in the s
### Added | - Real language servers (CS-6): `cli/test/lsp_real_servers.test.ts` runs the product's LSP client against typescript-language-server, pyright, rust-analyzer and gopls on a tiny fixture project (a deliberate error is reported; a clean file is a real empty report, not `unavailable`), skipping a server
### Fixed | - `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_hover` and `lsp_definition` never worked for TypeScript, JavaScript or Python files: the default commands started `typescript-language-server` and `pyright-langserver` without `--stdio`, so both exited at once and every query was `unavailable`. ### Added | - `scripts/gateway_conformance.mjs` and `docs/GATEWAY_CONFORMANCE.md` (MQ-4): a scheduled gateway conformance job for a local scheduler. It takes the `GATEWAY` claim without waiting (a held claim skips the run, exit 75), runs the unmodified tool-call matrix, judges each alias's native-valid ratio ag

A weakeni

### Added | - Tool-output masking (plan unit CX-4, opt-in): with `NEXUS_TOOL_OUTPUT_MASK_TOKENS=<n>`, a tool result larger than n estimated tokens that the model has already acted on is replaced in later requests by a short marker with a content id. ### Added | - Attempt lineage (plan unit VC-3, part): each verification attempt records its parent attempt and a hash of the step between candidate identities; `/requirements reference <R> <ref>` records an operator-named behavioural reference. The differential against it is not implemented

# Nexus Code v1.2.1

**Maturity:** the v1.2.1 plan ([`docs/v1.2.1/PLAN.md`](../v1.2.1/PLAN.md)) is landed except for the units listed under "Not in this release". **External qualification is pending.** This is not a claim that Nexus Code is frontier-grade. Every test, scenario and measurement named here is internal validation, and the figures are reported as measured, including the ones that miss. Candidate: [rc.2](v1.2.1-rc.2.md) (rc.1 was superseded: its release workflow failed on a test fixture and published no archive).

## What is in this release

- **More providers, as data and as native protocols.** Operators declare providers in `~/.config/nexus/providers.json` (validated: https only unless local, no credentials in URLs, header names and templates checked; the file is read from the operator's home, never from a project). A shipped catalog adds the OpenAI-compatible long tail. New native protocols: Gemini (`gemini-generate-content`), Amazon Bedrock Converse (`bedrock-converse`, SigV4 written on `node:crypto`, AWS event-stream framing, credentials from the 
- **Behaviour follows the model's listed capabilities.** `nexus models refresh` (the only command that contacts models.dev) validates and caches model data; context and output limits, tool-choice support and reasoning effort levels come from it and are never assumed when absent. Per-provider spending limits (`NEXUS_CLOUD_LIMITS`) price a provider that reports no cost from the snapshot, and refuse a cost limit that cannot be enforced.
- **Security.** Commands no longer inherit the process's credentials; `--sandbox` confines (HOME masked, no network unless asked); compaction summaries are labelled as untrusted data and checked against the gating requirements; the egress inspector refuses a network call that carries a workspace `.env` secret (its policy comes only from your environment, `NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY`, never from a repository file; commands behind `env`, `sudo`, `timeout`, `sh -c` and similar are inspected); a prompt-injection scanner label
- **Verification and review.** Operator-declared boundary rules enforced in the review gate; verification-file shell writes can be stopped (`verificationPaths.mode: "block"`); a repeated-call detector with a CERI scenario that fails when it is disabled; each compaction leaves an auditable record checked on resume; `verified` is re-checked on resume; the CERI evidence store checks resolved paths and run ids, and a baseline comparison binds model, sampling, fixture and evaluator identity before it can confirm a regre
- **Operations.** `nexus run --output stream-json` streams NDJSON events; a composite GitHub Action runs `nexus run --json` with a verification-gated exit code; `examples/` are tested; a weekly flake report records CI rerun events; a nightly real-project smoke job runs the headless CLI against synthetic representative repositories (a populated `node_modules`, a large Makefile reference graph, a deep tree, a pytest project) on a scripted mock gateway and goes red when a repository ends as anything but VERIFIED or RE
- **Maintainability.** `cli/src/agent.ts` is split along its seams (8,441 to 4,616 lines) with no test edited; the full suite's failing set is identical before and after.

## Behaviour changes to know about

- The egress inspector blocks a network command that carries a workspace secret by default (`NEXUS_EGRESS_POLICY` to relax it, in your own environment only).
- A tool result the injection scanner flags reaches the model fenced and labelled; the next step's state-changing calls ask you first (interactive only; headless and `--yes` get the label and fence only).
- A cost limit for a provider with no reported cost and no snapshot price is refused as unenforceable, as before; a malformed `NEXUS_CLOUD_LIMITS` refuses every cloud request.

## Not in this release

Deferred with a dated note in the plan: the Terminal-Bench/Harbor adapter and the false-completion report (MQ-1, MQ-2; no external measurement is published for this release), the scheduled gateway-conformance job (MQ-4; the gateway is not reachable from hosted runners), the macOS and arm64 artifacts (RD-1, RD-2), CI wall-time reduction to a measured median under 40 minutes (PC-1; PR runs took about 37 to 45 minutes), collapsing the redaction and terminal-safe variants (MT-3, part done), CERI slices D to G, per-comm

## Known limitations

- Nothing here is independent qualification.
- The injection scanner reads English phrasing and misses paraphrases, other languages, look-alike letters and text split by punctuation; see the User Manual for the measured rates.
- The egress inspector cannot see a secret a command builds at run time, one split across arguments, or one transformed beyond URL or base64 encoding.
- A revoked Vertex token keeps failing until it expires (no forced refresh after a 401); Vertex supports service-account key files and `gcloud` only.
- Live inference is the project's gateway only. The G1.1-4 tool-call validity measurement for this release is recorded in `docs/evidence/v1.2.1/` for the release candidate it was taken on; a measurement is valid only for its archive. The previous release did not meet the bar (`engineering/lead-reasoning` 155 of 200 on the published v1.2.0 archive).
------
# Nexus Code v1.2.1-rc.2 (release candidate)

**Maturity:** release candidate. Supersedes [`v1.2.1-rc.1`](v1.2.1-rc.1.md); the previous stable release is [`v1.2.0`](v1.2.0.md). This candidate carries the whole v1.2.1 scope and the stable release notes ([`v1.2.1.md`](v1.2.1.md)) together, because the release workflow requires a stable tag to be a version-only commit directly on its release candidate.

**Why rc.2 exists:** the release workflow for `v1.2.1-rc.1` failed in its CLI suite step and published no archive. One test (`cs4_shell_audit`, "exit 127 on runTestSuite names the scrub and the passthrough setting") assumed the verifier hint lists a given variable among at most twelve sorted names; on the release runner more than twelve toolchain-looking variables sort before it, so the test faile

What changed and what did not: see [`v1.2.1.md`](v1.2.1.md). Plan and per-unit status: [`docs/v1.2.1/PLAN.md`](../v1.2.1/PLAN.md).

Live-gateway tool-call validity for this candidate is recorded in the evidence file under [`docs/evidence/v1.2.1/`](../evidence/v1.2.1/) once measured (a measurement is only valid for the archive it was taken on). Until that file exists, no claim about it is made.

# Nexus Code v1.2.2

**Maturity:** the v1.2.2 backlog ([`docs/v1.2.2/BACKLOG.md`](../v1.2.2/BACKLOG.md)) is landed except for the units listed under "Not in this release". **External qualification is pending.** This is not a claim that Nexus Code is frontier-grade. Every test, scenario and measurement named here is internal validation, and the figures are reported as measured, including the ones that miss. Candidate: [rc.1](v1.2.2-rc.1.md).

## What is in this release

- **Containment.** Operator command rules (`~/.config/nexus/command_rules.json`, never read from a project): a shell command is `allow`ed without a prompt, `prompt`ed even in auto mode, or `forbidden` in every mode, and the deciding rule is recorded in the session export (CS-9, `docs/COMMAND_RULES.md`). With `--sandbox`, the native worker `harness-core` itself runs inside the sandbox, so a bug in it has the limits a command has: Bubblewrap, and on Linux Docker (CS-10). Whenever the worker is sandboxed, file, search, parse and git tools go to a second worker that refuses to run commands and has no network even with `--sandbox-network`. The implementer and tester roles are refused the tools that reach outside the task (VC-8). Transient delegated children run under an authority that is the intersection of the parent's, the profile's and the session's.
- **MCP and plugin tools work.** They were offered to the model but never registered, so every call answered `FAIL-001: Tool ... is not registered` and the server never received `tools/call`. They are now registered as `extension` capabilities after connection.
- **Headless runs end with a question instead of stalling.** A headless run that needs a decision nobody is there to make ends `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT` with a machine-readable question and resumes with `--answer`. This release covers a write, command or egress approval, a verification-file edit, the verifier or type-check at completion, a delegated subagent's question, a requirement the model marks blocked (answered in free text, `--answer <id>=reply:<text>`) and steering that would drop a requirement and went undecided (VC-9).
- **Verification and review.** Operator-authorised regression obligations are replayed by every later attempt and block completion while unmet (VC-2); type-check errors that newly appear in a file the task never touched block completion (VC-6); the convergence stop also applies to verifier commands run through `run_tests` (VC-7); `/requirements differential` runs a reference command against the verifier on operator inputs (VC-3); significant independent reviews require eight engineering-assessment fields; a command that fails with only volatile text changing counts as the same failure (CS-11).
- **Context.** Opt-in tool-output masking (`NEXUS_TOOL_OUTPUT_MASK_TOKENS`, CX-4): measured on three large-output tasks, all 30 runs passed and median prompt tokens fell 42 to 61% at 2000; kept opt-in because one model and tasks that all passed cannot show where masking would lose evidence (`docs/evidence/v1.2.2/CX-4-masking-measurement.md`). `@path` imports in project instruction files (CX-7). Opt-in Anthropic prompt-cache hints (CX-6, not validated against the live API).
- **Sessions.** `/fork` and `--fork-session` continue in a copy of a session; a worktree-bound session is refused a fork rather than silently creating a second checkout (RD-6). A worktree binding carried into a later turn is now re-established instead of failing the save when the workspace path looks like a secret.
- **Language servers.** `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_hover` and `lsp_definition` never worked for TypeScript, JavaScript or Python (the servers were started without `--stdio` and exited at once); fixed. Rust diagnostics no longer report a file with type errors as clean. A weekly real-server job runs typescript, python, go and rust (CS-6).
- **Operations and CI.** A scheduled gateway conformance job and its claim and alert protocol (MQ-4, `docs/GATEWAY_CONFORMANCE.md`). Median PR CI time is 27 minutes 12 seconds over the first 20 runs after the CLI suite was sharded inside the existing jobs, against 42 minutes 19 seconds before (PC-1, `docs/evidence/v1.2.2/PC-1_POST_SHARDING_2026-11-21.md`). `nexus uninstall` for managed installations (RD-7).
- **Also on this release, from the v1.3.0 track (not part of the v1.2.2 backlog).** `/batch` runs a validated dependency graph of work units on the operation engine, and parallel operation work is admitted by resource budget (`docs/v1.3.0/`). They are in this release because they are on `main`; their status is the one recorded in those documents.

## Behaviour changes to know about

- In `nexus run`, a requirement the model marks blocked now ends the run `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT` (exit code still 1, task status `failed`) instead of `COMPLETED / REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`. The REPL, the sidecar and library callers are unchanged.
- On Linux, `--sandbox docker` runs the worker inside the container and refuses to start it outside one. Commands in one session share that container's `/tmp`; before, each command got a fresh container. Elsewhere Docker still confines commands only (`nexus doctor` says which applies).
- Steering that would drop a requirement and got no decision before its turn ended now ends that turn `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT`.
- The implementer and tester roles no longer have the browser tools or `manage_knowledge`; the tester also loses `fetch_web`, `search_web` and `spawn_subagent`.

## Not in this release

Deferred with a dated note in the backlog: the false-completion benchmark and its report (MQ-1, MQ-2; no external measurement is published for this release), macOS and arm64 artifacts (RD-1, RD-2), live validation of the Anthropic and Bedrock cache path (CX-6), the steering semantic judge (VC-10), splitting the two large TUI source files (MT-2), and a default threshold for tool-output masking (CX-4).

## Known limitations

- Nothing here is independent qualification.
- Live inference is the project's gateway only. The first scheduled conformance run, on the published v1.2.1 archive, was **not conformant**: `engineering/deep` 200 of 200 native-valid, but `engineering/lead-reasoning` 155 of 200 (77.5%), `edit_file` 5 of 50, the same count as the earlier run on that archive. The gateway serves two distinct models, so its five aliases are two models (`docs/evidence/v1.2.2/WM-3-gateway-aliases.md`). The measurement for this release is recorded under `docs/evidence/v1.2.2/` for the release candidate it was taken on; a measurement is only valid for its archive. Until that file exists, no claim about it is made.
- The Docker worker depends on starting the host-built binary through its own loader and libraries inside the container image; it is covered by tests on a Linux host with a Docker daemon and on the hosted runner. A container that fails to start surfaces as a worker disconnect.
- The files-only worker's refusal to run commands is a check inside the process; what holds if that process is compromised is its sandbox (no network, no path outside the workspace). The two workers share the workspace.
- A blocked-requirement or steering-conflict answer lives in the invoking process; a new objective starts a new ledger, so an old conflict can no longer be answered. The Rust TUI shows the blocked turn but has no key for the sidecar `answer` command.
- The CI timing sample is one four-hour window; eight of its 20 executions were failed runs, which finish sooner.

Rust diagnostics no longer report a file with type errors as clean. A weekly real-server job runs typescript, python, go and rust (CS-6).
- **Operations and CI.** A scheduled gateway conformance job and its claim and alert protocol (MQ-4, `docs/GATEWAY_CONFORMANCE.md`). Median PR CI time is 27 minutes 12 seconds over the first 20 runs after the CLI suite was sharded inside the existing jobs, against 42 minutes 19 seconds before (PC-1, `docs/evidence/v1.2.2/PC-1_POST_SHARDING_2026-11-21.md`). `nexus uninstall` for managed installations (RD-7).
- **Also on this release, from the v1.3.0 track (not part of the v1.2.2 backlog).** `/batch` runs a validated dependency graph of work units on the operation engine, and parallel operation work is admitted by resource budget (`docs/v1.3.0/`). They are in this release because they are on `main`; their status is the one recorded in those documents.

## Behaviour changes to know about

- In `nexus run`, a requirement the model marks blocked now ends the run `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT` (exit code still 1, task status `failed`) instead of `COMPLETED / REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`. The REPL, the sidecar and library callers are unchanged.
- On Linux, `--sandbox docker` runs the worker inside the container and refuses to start it outside one. Commands in one session share that container's `/tmp`; before, each command got a fresh container. Elsewhere Docker still confines commands only (`nexus doctor` says which applies).
- Steering that would drop a requirement and got no decision before its turn ended now ends that turn `BLOCKED / NEEDS_INPUT`.
- The implementer and tester roles no longer have the browser tools or `manage_knowledge`; the tester also loses `fetch_web`, `search_web` and `spawn_subagent`.

## Not in this release

Deferred with a dated note in the backlog: the false-completion benchmark and its report (MQ-1, MQ-2; no external measurement is published for this release), macOS and arm64 artifacts (RD-1, RD-2), live validation of the Anthropic and Bedrock cache path (CX-6), the steering semantic judge (VC-10), splitting the two large TUI source files (MT-2), and a default threshold for tool-output masking (CX-4).

## Known limitations

- Nothing here is independent qualification.
- Live inference is the project's gateway only. The first scheduled conformance run, on the published v1.2.1 archive, was **not conformant**: `engineering/deep` 200 of 200 native-valid, but `engineering/lead-reasoning` 155 of 200 (77.5%), `edit_file` 5 of 50, the same count as the earlier run on that archive. The gateway serves two distinct models, so its five aliases are two models (`docs/evidence/v1.2.2/WM-3-gateway-aliases.md`). The measurement for this release is recorded under `docs/evidence/v1.2.2/` for the release candidate it was taken on; a measurement is only valid for its archive. Until that file exists, no claim about it is made.
- The Docker worker depends on starting the host-built binary through its own loader and libraries inside the container image; it is covered by tests on a Linux host with a Docker daemon and on the hosted runner. A container that fails to start surfaces as a worker disconnect.
- The files-only worker's refusal to run commands is a check inside the process; what holds if that process is compromised is its sandbox (no network, no path outside the workspace). The two workers share the workspace.
- A blocked-requirement or steering-conflict answer lives in the invoking process; a new objective starts a new ledger, so an old conflict can no longer be answered. The Rust TUI shows the blocked turn but has no key for the sidecar `answer` command.
- The CI timing sample is one four-hour window; eight of its 20 executions were failed runs, which finish sooner.

CS-10 is merged and the release candidate is prepared locally; nothing is tagged. v1.2.2 is not released.

- **Gate items:** all of them are now on `main`. Codex merged CS-10 (#671) as `92b3d77a`, and a probe I ran showed the Docker worker now starts on the hosted runner, which it never did before. VC-9, CS-6, CX-4 and PC-1 were already merged.
- **#679 (new, mine):** a small fix for an uncaught `EPIPE` crash when a worker exits right after launch, which a failing Docker container would trigger. Its new test fails without the fix (3 of 3 runs) and passes with it. On current `main` the `sandbox_quoting` flake I saw earlier didn't reproduce in 12 runs, and the PR text says so. I used a file Codex still holds a claim on, since that work is merged and the holder is idle; I logged it and Codex can object.
- **Release candidate, local only:** one commit on a branch, `ed7a3f64`. It bumps every package to 1.2.2-rc.1 and adds the RC and stable release notes, written from the changelog and the evidence files with the misses stated (lead-reasoning at 155 of 200 on the v1.2.1 archive, external qualification pending). The doc-version and version-sync checks pass.
- **The flooded-environment suite is the pre-tag check.** It runs the full CLI suite with 29 toolchain-style variables set, the condition that broke v1.2.1's first RC. It's running now, and the candidate waits on it.
- **A scope fact for you:** `main` also carries v1.3.0 track work that will ship in this release: `/batch`, parallel operation admission and enforced delegation authority. The notes list them separately and keep the docs' "qualification pending" wording. If you'd rather gate or exclude them, say so before the tag.

Next, in order:
1. #679's checks and `main`'s CI on the CS-10 merge finish.
2. I merge #679 and bring it into the release branch.
3. I open the release-prep PR, merge it once green, and tag a signed `v1.2.2-rc.1`, which your earlier answer authorised. The release workflow takes about an hour.
4. I run the tool-call matrix on the published archive for `deep` and `lead-reasoning`. Stable is tagged only if it meets the 99.5% bar, and not without your go-ahead.

A watch fires when #679's checks and `main`'s CI settle.

content.text:
v1.2.2 is not released and nothing is tagged. All your gate items are on `main`, and the release-candidate cut is now in Codex's hands, not mine.

## Where the release stands
- **Gate items:** VC-9, CS-6, CX-4, PC-1 and CS-10 are all merged. My EPIPE fix (#679) is also merged, as `0941e6d9`.
- **The release candidate is Codex's.** It took over the RC claim at 17:25, recorded as owner-authorised, and is continuing on the branch I prepared (my version-bump and release-notes commit, plus one of its own aligning the notes with the backlog). I won't push or tag it. No `v1.2.2` tag exists yet, and the RC pull request hasn't been opened.

## What I found with the pre-tag check
I ran the full CLI suite under a runner-like environment, the condition that broke v1.2.1's first RC. It turned up one real defect.

- **A failing type-check could stop blocking completion.** With `FORCE_COLOR=1` in your environment, the type-checker colours its output, the parser finds no file in it, and the failure is classified `ENVIRONMENT` ("could not run") instead of `FAILED`.
- **Fix:** PR #681 strips colour codes before parsing. Its new test, built from real coloured `tsc` output, fails 3 of 4 without the fix and passes 4 of 4 with it. The two affected suites failed 5 and 4 tests under `FORCE_COLOR=1` and now pass both ways.
- **Release impact:** no workflow sets `FORCE_COLOR`, so CI and the release run aren't affected. Operators who export it are. I think it should land before the RC tag and logged that for Codex.
- **The other failures in that run were not product defects:** the eval suites and the SBOM tool fail on this host for known local reasons, and one test failed only under load.

The release-prep PR for `v1.2.2-rc.1` is open as #683 and its CI is running. Nothing is tagged yet, and v1.2.2 is not released.

## What happened
- **#681 merged** as `8e4214df`: the fix for a coloured type-check failure being read as "could not run".
- **I took the RC back from Codex.** Its claim had sat idle for two hours with the branch unpushed, while `main` gained four more merges. I logged the takeover with the reason, the same way Codex had taken it from me, and asked it to say so if it was mid-edit. You authorised me to cut `rc.1`.
- **What #683 contains:**
  - The 1.2.2-rc.1 version bump across all five version files.
  - The RC and stable release notes, including Codex's commit that corrected one of my claims about session forking.
  - Changelog entries for the three late fixes.
  - A correction to a backlog row that still said Cargo was excluded from the type-check baseline.
- **Checks so far:** the doc-version, version-sync and requirements checks pass. The release-specific tests pass against binaries built from this tree.

## In flight
- **#683's three required checks.**
- **A second full suite under a runner-like environment**, this time without the two settings that produced false failures in the first run.

## Next, in order
1. Merge #683 when its checks are green at the exact head and `main` is green.
2. Wait for `main`'s CI on the merge commit.
3. Tag a signed `v1.2.2-rc.1` there and push it. The release workflow takes about an hour.
4. Run the tool-call matrix on the published archive for `deep` and `lead-reasoning` and record the result unaltered.

Stable is tagged only if the RC meets the 99.5% bar, and not without your go-ahead.

## Still your call

- v1.2.2 itself is unaffected: it merges into `main` and is tagged as planned.

Branch worktrees from it, open every PR against it, and do not merge any PR into `main`.
- `main` receives one merge, from the release branch, when the release is ready to be tagged (the release workflow requires the tagged commit to be an ancestor of `main`).
- CI gaps to close on that branch when it is created: `ci.yml` runs on `push` only for `main` (add the release branch so post-merge CI still runs), and `codeql.yml` only covers PRs into `main` and `v1/integration`. `pull_request` CI has no branch filter, so the three required checks already run for PRs targeting any base.
- Other agents learn of it through the claims log; the notice and its correction are logged there (2026-11-21). Put the rule in `AGENTS.md` on the release branch when it is created.
- When the owner gives a process rule mid-release, check whether it applies now or from the next release before acting; I acted immediately and had to undo it.

Owner instruction, 2026-11-21 (verbatim): "from now on, nothing gets merged into main until the release is ready to be tagged. a master release branch is to be created and all development work lands on that release branch until it is ready to be merged to main." Clarified minutes later: "I meant after v1.2.2 lands".

## Workflow

### Plan
- Plan any non-trivial task (3+ steps or an architectural decision) before building: write the plan to `tasks/todo.md` as checkable items and check in before implementing. Plan the verification steps too.
- When something goes sideways, stop and re-plan at once.
- Tick items off as you go, give a high-level summary of each change, and end with a review section in `tasks/todo.md`.

### Subagents
- Keep the main context clean: offload research, exploration and parallel analysis to subagents, one tack per subagent. Throw more subagents at a complex problem.

### Lessons
- After any user correction, add the pattern to `tasks/lessons.md` as a rule that prevents the same mistake, and iterate until the mistake rate drops. Review the file at session start.

### Done means proven
- A task is complete when evidence shows it works: tests run, logs checked, behaviour diffed against main where relevant. Ask: would a staff engineer approve this?

### Elegance
- For a non-trivial change, pause and look for a more elegant way; when a fix feels hacky, implement the elegant solution with everything you now know. Keep simple, obvious fixes simple. Challenge your own work before presenting it.

### Bug reports
- Fix them from the evidence: logs, errors, failing tests, CI failures included. Resolve without being walked through it.

## Principles
- **Simplicity first**: the smallest change that works, touching only what is necessary.
- **Root cause**: no temporary fixes; senior-developer standard.

@RTK.md

# graphify
`/graphify` → invoke the Skill tool with `skill: "graphify"` (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) before anything else.

# RTK (Rust Token Killer)

A hook rewrites shell commands through `rtk` (60-90% fewer tokens): write ordinary commands (`git status` runs as `rtk git status`).

- Raw output: `rtk proxy <cmd>`. Use it to debug, and whenever a rewritten `grep`, `awk` or `sed` pipeline returns filtered or odd output; rerun it raw before trusting it.
- Savings: `rtk gain`, `rtk gain --history`. Missed opportunities: `rtk discover`.
- If `rtk gain` fails, a different `rtk` is installed (reachingforthejack/rtk, Rust Type Kit); check `which rtk`.

## Principles

1. Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.
2. Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.
3. Touch only what you must. Clean up only your mess.
4. Define success criteria. Loop until verified.

## Agent workflow

Specialised agents live in `~/.claude/agents/` (their descriptions are in the agent list). Delegate any feature, bug fix or significant change to **`@orchestrator`**: it runs the pipeline and returns one structured summary (changes, test results, review findings, issues) while the verbose output stays in its context.

Pipeline: `@architect` plans and identifies affected files → `@coder` writes code (linter only, no tests) → `@tester` writes and runs tests, looping with coder on failures → `@reviewer` reviews the final diff (security, performance, readability, consistency) → `@design-qa` screenshots affected pages at mobile, tablet and desktop (UI changes only).

Call a single agent directly for one stage: architect, coder, tester, reviewer, design-qa, security-auditor, migration-planner (alembic, sqlite3), api-designer, ci-validator (GitLab CI).

Handle these yourself, without delegating: codebase questions, reading and explaining code, git operations, deployments, config changes.

Affected tests across all sub-projects (Go, Playwright, pytest): `./scripts/verify.sh` (the tester agent uses it).

## Browsing

Use the gstack `/browse` skill for all web browsing, and keep `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools out of use.

## Sub-projects

| Project | Stack | Location |
|---------|-------|----------|
| SyndicateCode | Go 1.25, bubbletea TUI, gRPC, sqlite3 | `./SyndicateCode/` |
| aisyndicate | Next.js 16, React, TypeScript, Radix UI | `./aisyndicate/` |
| syndicateclaw | Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, alembic | `./syndicateclaw/` |
| controlplane-enterprise | Go, enterprise control plane | `./controlplane-enterprise/` |
| syndicategate | Go, backend service | `./syndicategate/` |

## graphify

`graphify-out/` holds a knowledge graph (god nodes, communities, cross-file relationships).

- For a codebase question, start with `graphify query "<question>"` when `graphify-out/graph.json` exists; use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for one concept. Each returns a scoped subgraph, usually far smaller than `GRAPH_REPORT.md` or raw grep.
- Navigate broadly through `graphify-out/wiki/index.md` when it exists.
- Read `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` for broad architecture review, or when query, path and explain fall short.
- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` (AST-only, no API cost).
@AGENTS.md

# nexus-code agent guide

TypeScript CLI (`cli/`), Rust core (`core/`), eval harness (`eval/`). Current plans: `docs/v1.2.1/PLAN.md`, then `docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md`. Per-release records live in `docs/releases/` and `docs/evidence/`.

## Build and test
- Build: `make build` (core, then `tsc` in `cli/`). Everything: `make test`; the CI-equivalent run: `make test-ci`. Lint the core with `cargo clippy`; `cli/` has no lint script, `npm --prefix cli run build` type-checks it.
- One TypeScript test file: `cd cli && HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/<name>.test.ts`. A throwaway `HOME` is mandatory: a test that touched the real `HOME` once overwrote `~/.config/nexus/config.env`.
- Done = the affected test files pass, plus `tsc` for TypeScript changes. CI is the arbiter; a failure that appears only locally comes from host state first (an unbuilt `cli/dist` or Rust core, a stray `/tmp/.git`), so rule that out before calling it a defect.
- Test-runner or process-handling changes run on Node 22 and 24: the two emit different `node:test` events.
- Rust builds use an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree.
- Preserve existing comments and unrelated changes.
- Entire CLI: export `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file` before any `entire` command. The Entire gate no longer counts toward merging.

## Reference coding with XERJ (required)
- Before writing non-trivial code that has a peer-project analogue (feature, protocol, parser, worktree or provider handling, tool, test harness), read what mature projects do: query the local XERJ node, then record what you took, borrowed or rejected in the PR's "Reference coding" section. Exempt: trivial edits, doc-only changes, fixes fully specified by a failing test.
- Node, commands, corpora, licence and privacy rules, the field report, and the fallback when XERJ is unavailable ("XERJ unavailable: <reason>" plus `git grep`): `docs/XERJ_REFERENCE_CODING.md`. Read it when you start that first query.

## Concurrency, claims and release authority
- Several agents can work here: follow `docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md`. Claim a slice or hot file under `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` before editing; one worktree and branch per slice (`~/nexus-wt/`), never `~/nexus-code` itself; isolate `HOME` for every test or probe; stop a process by its own pid, never `pkill -f`; check `git log` for foreign commits before each commit.
- Take the `GATEWAY` claim for any inference run; the key comes from the environment (`~/.config/nexus/config.env`) and is never printed. The gateway is the only live provider.
- Push, tag and publish only on an explicit owner instruction; release authority is the owner's.

## Merging and releasing
Bias to correct: a green PR is not a green `main`, and a pushed tag cannot be taken back.
- When merging: required checks are `test-matrix (22)`, `test-matrix (24)`, `linux-x86_64`; read each check's conclusion (empty or in-progress is not success). Merge with a merge commit, `gh pr merge <n> --merge --match-head-commit <full-sha>`. PRs that touch one subsystem merge one at a time, each followed by the CI run on `main`: two PRs green alone can break `main` together.
- When a PR's checks look wrong after `main` moved: PR checks run on GitHub's merge commit, so confirm the run checked out the current `merge_commit_sha` (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> --jq .merge_commit_sha`); a stale one tests old content.
- When cutting a stable release: make a version-only commit directly on the accepted RC (`node scripts/check-version-only-diff.mjs <rc-ref> <stable-ref>`), land it on `main` through a merge-commit PR, and only then tag, because `release.yml` requires the tagged commit to be an ancestor of `main`. Version tags are immutable: re-run a failed run, or move to the next RC or patch. Then follow `docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md`.
- When reporting a gate or a result: state it as measured ("ledger closed, qualification pending"), record failed runs unaltered, and make no frontier-grade claim without external qualification.
- Before tagging or merging, check: required checks green at the exact head? CI on `main` green after the previous merge? Tagged commit an ancestor of `main`? Claims match the evidence?
